moat_against: ADP has greater scale and enterprise reach
Cloud-native competitors innovate faster at the UI layer at both SMB and mid-market ends
Growth capped by SMB employment growth; a soft labor market hits client counts directly
Interest on client funds is rate-sensitive — Fed cuts shrink that earnings stream
Paycor integration/synergy execution ($80M+ targeted) not yet proven on an organic basis
Acquisition debt (net debt $3,467,900,000) replaced a previously near-unlevered balance sheet
moat_for: High switching costs — payroll/tax compliance is mission-critical and embedded in client workflows
Recurring revenue with durable retention through cycles
PEO co-employment model raises lock-in and lifetime value (ASO-to-PEO conversions ~2x plan in Q1 FY2027)
Scale + direct distribution + bundled HCM/benefits/retirement/insurance stack
Proven pricing power with ~44% adjusted operating margins
Client-funds float is a structural earnings kicker while rates stay higher
moat_justification: Payroll is mission-critical and compliance-laden, making switching painful and retention durable; the PEO co-employment model deepens lock-in. Scale, direct distribution, and a bundled HR/benefits/retirement stack give proven pricing power (~44% adjusted operating margins held through cycles). Not wide: ADP is larger with greater enterprise reach, cloud-native rivals innovate faster at the product layer, per-employee pricing is exposed to SMB employment levels and AI automation, client-funds income is rate-sensitive, and Paycor synergies are not yet proven organically. Prior run scored 6/10 on the same facts; the range does not change the tier.
name: Paychex, Inc.
one_liner: Strong payroll/HCM franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $106.25 it clears only a 9.1% weighted IRR (IV@15 $54.10) on guided 5-6% organic growth; Tier D, needs ~$54 to clear 15%.
